The agreed scope states which sessions are included; it should never rely on an assumption that a single camera operator can be in several places at once.

faqs.question: Is livestreaming included with conference filming?
faqs.answer: Recording a session and broadcasting it live are different requirements. Livestreaming needs its own platform, connectivity, production and testing plan. If you need it, include that in the initial brief so feasibility, responsibilities and costs can be assessed with the venue. A conference recording package should not be treated as a promise of a live broadcast unless the proposal explicitly includes it.

faqs.question: How do you capture clear audio and presentation slides?
faqs.answer: We coordinate with the venue or AV contact on microphone coverage, sound-feed access and how presentation material will be supplied or captured. Audience questions and panel speakers need particular attention because the recording depends on their audio too. Slides and speaker names should be provided in an agreed format. The setup is reviewed before the sessions covered by the production scope begin.

faqs.question: How soon will the finished videos be ready?
faqs.answer: The schedule depends on the number of recordings, interviews, graphics, caption requirements and finished versions. A short recap and a large session library have different editing workloads. We agree delivery milestones and review dates before the event. If a particular clip is time-sensitive, flag it early so the production and editing plan can account for that priority.

faqs.question: What should we send to request a quote?
faqs.answer: Send your event date, venue, draft agenda, room count and the videos you want afterward. Include the venue AV contact if available, any livestreaming requirement, deadlines and approximate interview needs. Share examples to explain the intended style, along with access or speaker restrictions. We can then identify missing details and put together a scope for coverage, editing and delivery.

faqs.question: Can head office keep control while local managers contribute?
faqs.answer: Yes. We define central brand standards and approval responsibilities, then give local teams a clear way to supply information and request changes. The process can cover photos, service updates, offers, events and customer questions. The aim is useful local participation with visible accountability, rather than either unrestricted changes or a central bottleneck.

faqs.question: Do all locations need the same marketing budget?
faqs.answer: No. Budget decisions should reflect local demand, competition, maturity, commercial priorities and the capacity to serve more customers. A new opening may need a different approach from a location that already has a full appointment book. We agree the criteria for reviewing spend and use available branch outcomes to guide changes.

faqs.question: How do you prevent locations from competing for the same enquiries?
faqs.answer: We review service areas, campaign targeting, location pages and routing rules together. Where coverage overlaps, your business needs a clear rule for assigning enquiries and handling customer choice. The appropriate setup depends on the services and geography. We then check the actual enquiry paths and use reporting to identify conflicts or misplaced leads.

faqs.question: Can you work with franchisees and company-owned branches together?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scope should reflect the different ownership and approval arrangements. We agree which accounts, budgets and assets are centrally managed and what each local operator is responsible for. Reporting also needs consistent definitions, while recognizing that available systems and commercial priorities may differ across the network.

faqs.question: Will every location get its own page and Google Business Profile?
faqs.answer: Useful location pages can help customers find the correct services and contact details, but their content should reflect real local information. Business Profile eligibility is a separate question governed by Google’s requirements. We review the actual locations and operating model rather than creating duplicate profiles or treating every service area as a physical branch.

faqs.question: What do you need to price a multi-location marketing program?
faqs.answer: Share the number of locations, ownership structure, priority markets, current channels and the problems you want to solve. We also need to understand account access, existing content, reporting systems and the role of your internal team. The proposal can separate shared setup, per-location work, ongoing management, production and advertising spend so the costs are understandable.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Seller Central and Vendor Central?
faqs.answer: Seller Central supports third-party businesses that sell products to shoppers on Amazon. Vendor Central supports an invitation-only first-party relationship in which a business sells products wholesale to Amazon. The difference affects commercial control, operations and reporting. We first confirm which model you use so the proposed work addresses the account you actually have.

faqs.question: Can you get our brand invited to Vendor Central?
faqs.answer: No consultant can guarantee an invitation. Amazon decides which businesses it invites and the terms of that relationship. Our service focuses on supporting an existing account and helping your team assess its operational and commercial options. If your business is not a vendor, Seller Central may be the relevant account model to discuss.

faqs.question: Can you help with chargebacks, shortages and deductions?
faqs.answer: We can review the information available, organize supporting records and help prepare an agreed issue-handling process. The scope depends on the type of deduction, the account history and the evidence your business can provide. Amazon decides the outcome of disputes, so the proposal should describe the review and follow-up work without promising a recovery amount.

faqs.question: Do you provide advice or manage ongoing account tasks?
faqs.answer: Either can be scoped. A consulting engagement may focus on assessment and recommendations, while ongoing support includes specified execution and reporting. We define which tasks Elatre handles, what your team supplies and who approves commercial decisions. Purchase-order commitments, finance decisions and supply obligations need clear ownership within your business.

faqs.question: Can you support Vendor Central and Seller Central together?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can review both parts of the business and coordinate the agreed scope. The plan needs to reflect your actual account permissions, products, costs and operational arrangements. We do not assume that every product should use both models or that one model is always better. The decision should be based on the business case and applicable account conditions.

faqs.question: How is Amazon Vendor Central consulting priced?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on the number of products and markets, the condition of the account records, the operational issue backlog and the work you want us to execute. A focused account review differs from ongoing catalog, campaign and reporting support. Share your main concerns and current team structure so we can propose deliverables, dependencies and fees clearly.

faqs.question: Can you test software built by another company?
faqs.answer: Yes. We need suitable access, a description of the intended behavior and someone who can answer product questions. Existing test cases and technical documentation are helpful but do not need to be perfect. We identify missing information and environment dependencies at the start, then agree what can be evaluated reliably within the scope.

faqs.question: Should we choose manual testing or test automation?
faqs.answer: Most products benefit from a considered mix. Automation suits stable checks that need to run repeatedly. Manual and exploratory testing help investigate new behavior, confusing interactions and cases that are not fully understood yet. We choose the approach around risk, frequency and maintenance effort, rather than assuming that automating every possible action is the best use of the budget.

faqs.question: How do you work with our developers across time zones?
faqs.answer: We agree meeting overlap, backlog access, defect-reporting standards and response responsibilities before the first cycle. Clear steps and evidence allow developers to investigate without waiting for a call. Scheduled triage resolves priority questions, while an escalation route handles blockers. The proposal identifies the actual working arrangement rather than making an undefined promise of constant availability.

faqs.question: What does a software testing report include?
faqs.answer: A useful report identifies the build and environment, scope, executed cases, significant findings, retest status and areas that could not be checked. Defects include steps to reproduce, expected and actual behavior, severity and appropriate evidence. The release summary explains remaining risks so the responsible owner can make a decision with the limitations visible.

faqs.question: Who owns the automated tests and testing materials?
faqs.answer: Ownership and access are agreed in the contract. The handover should name the scripts, cases, documentation and reports included, together with any tool licenses or account dependencies. We also document how to run and maintain the checks. That makes the testing work useful to your team after the initial engagement ends.

faqs.question: Can software testing guarantee a product has no bugs?
faqs.answer: No. Testing provides evidence about behavior within a defined scope and set of conditions. Complex software can still contain defects outside that coverage or under conditions not yet observed. We make the important risks, unresolved findings and coverage limits clear, then recommend where additional testing would be most useful before or after release.

faqs.question: How much does a home improvement marketing agency cost?
faqs.answer: The cost depends on the number of services and locations, the condition of your website and accounts, the content needed and the level of ongoing management. Advertising spend is separate from agency fees unless the proposal explicitly says otherwise. Share your priority services, coverage area, current lead volume and budget so we can recommend a scope with clear deliverables.

faqs.question: Should we start with SEO, Google Ads or Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: Start with the problem you need to solve. Search advertising may help reach active demand while SEO and service content improve discoverability over time. Local Services Ads is an option only where your business and category qualify. We also check your pages and enquiry handling, because additional traffic has limited value when people cannot get a useful response.

faqs.question: Can you help us attract larger or better-fit projects?
faqs.answer: Yes, the work can focus on the services, project types and locations you want to prioritize. That may mean different examples, more useful service information, clearer qualification questions and changes to campaign targeting. We agree what a good enquiry looks like with your team and review actual opportunities rather than treating every form submission as equally valuable.

faqs.question: Can you work with our existing scheduling or field-service software?
faqs.answer: We begin by reviewing the system, its available integrations and the workflow you need. Some improvements use existing features; others may require an integration or a separate development scope. The aim is to route enquiries and record outcomes clearly while preserving a reliable source of truth for jobs, customer records and scheduling.

faqs.question: How soon should we expect results?
faqs.answer: Timing depends on the starting point and the work involved. Correcting a broken form is different from building local organic visibility or changing a long sales cycle. We agree launch milestones and useful early indicators, then measure qualified enquiries and booked work as data becomes available. A responsible proposal explains dependencies rather than promising a fixed number of jobs by a particular date.

faqs.question: Can you create our project photos, videos and customer stories?
faqs.answer: Yes. Elatre has photography, videography and editing capabilities that can support the marketing scope. We agree locations, access, contributors, permissions and the final asset list before production. Existing material can also be reviewed and repurposed. The content should show real work and useful customer questions, with filming arrangements and production costs made clear.

faqs.question: What does manufacturing video production include?
faqs.answer: A project can cover planning, scripting or interview questions, filming, editing, sound, graphics, captions and final exports. The exact mix depends on the purpose. A plant overview and a technical product demonstration need different footage and review. Your proposal sets out the locations, filming time, finished videos, formats and revision process so the scope is clear before production starts.

faqs.question: Can you film while our facility is operating?
faqs.answer: We can plan filming around the operating conditions you approve. Your facility team decides what access is permitted and what induction, protective equipment or supervision is required. We agree camera positions and production windows before the shoot. Some shots may need a separate window or an alternative approach; we do not assume that every activity can be filmed safely during normal operation.

faqs.question: Can you edit footage our team already has?
faqs.answer: Yes. We first review sample files for picture quality, sound, available angles and usage rights. We also check whether the footage actually answers the intended question. Existing material may support a complete edit, or it may need a short interview, updated product shots or simple graphics. That assessment helps avoid paying for filming that is unnecessary while identifying gaps early.

faqs.question: How do you handle confidential products and processes?
faqs.answer: We agree the restricted areas, screens, drawings, customer information and unfinished products before filming. Your team identifies anything that must stay out of the shot, and the technical review checks the edit before release. Where needed, confidentiality terms form part of the agreement. The published version should show only the information your authorized reviewer has approved.

faqs.question: How long does a manufacturing video project take?
faqs.answer: Timing depends on access, preparation, filming, animation and review. A project using approved existing footage differs from a shoot across several facilities. Product availability and internal approvals can affect the schedule as much as editing. Share your required launch date at the start, and we will propose a sequence of planning, production and review milestones around the confirmed scope.

faqs.question: Can one shoot provide content for several channels?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the different uses are planned before filming. A website film, a silent exhibition loop and a vertical social clip need different framing, text and pacing. We list the required versions in the brief and capture suitable material. B2B video production can also connect the project with product demonstrations, interviews and sales content, without assuming that a single edit will work everywhere.

faqs.question: What is adaptive AI in practical terms?
faqs.answer: It is an approach to improving an AI system as relevant information or operating conditions change. The implementation may use feedback, updated knowledge, revised decision rules or model retraining. The useful question is what can change, how the change is tested and who approves it. An adaptive system should have a defined improvement process rather than a vague promise to get smarter.

faqs.question: Does the system learn automatically from every conversation?
faqs.answer: It does not have to, and that is usually too broad a starting assumption. Feedback may be incorrect, incomplete or contain information that should not be reused. We define which sources can inform improvements, how examples are reviewed and whether a change requires approval. Production updates should follow the controls agreed for the workflow.

faqs.question: Can you work with an AI system we already have?
faqs.answer: Yes. We begin by reviewing the application, model providers, data access and current performance information. Some improvements can be made around the existing system, such as better evaluation or knowledge updates. Others may need changes to integration or architecture. We identify those dependencies before recommending whether to extend the current implementation or replace a specific component.

faqs.question: How do you decide whether to update knowledge or retrain a model?
faqs.answer: We investigate the cause of the problem. Outdated facts may need a refreshed knowledge source. A workflow error may need a rule or integration fix. Retraining is a different decision and needs suitable data, evaluation and operating support. Comparing the options helps avoid an expensive model change when a smaller correction would address the issue.

faqs.question: How do you know that an update is actually better?
faqs.answer: Compare it with the current version using representative cases and agreed measures. Those can include task completion, important error types, human review, response time and cost. We also look for regressions on cases that previously worked. A controlled rollout can provide further evidence, with a defined route to restore the previous version if results deteriorate.

faqs.question: What affects the cost and delivery schedule?
faqs.answer: The starting system, data quality, available feedback, number of integrations and release controls all affect the work. A knowledge-refresh workflow is different from a predictive model that needs labeled data and retraining infrastructure. We scope the initial assessment, implementation and ongoing responsibilities separately, so you can see both the build cost and the commitment needed after launch.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an AI proof of concept and an AI MVP?
faqs.answer: A proof of concept tests a technical question, such as whether a model can extract the information you need from a document. A prototype explores the interaction. An MVP combines enough of the real product for intended users to complete a useful task. We choose the starting point based on the uncertainty you need to resolve.

faqs.question: Can you help us decide whether our product needs AI?
faqs.answer: Yes. We compare the proposed AI capability with the current process and simpler approaches. The question is whether AI adds enough value to justify its variability, running cost and maintenance. Some products benefit from a small AI feature inside an otherwise conventional application. Others need a feasibility test before a product build makes sense.

faqs.question: What do we need to provide before work starts?
faqs.answer: Bring a description of the user and task, examples of the inputs and desired outputs, and details of the systems involved. A product owner and someone who understands the subject matter should be available for decisions. If data access or quality is unresolved, we identify that dependency before committing to a development schedule.

faqs.question: How much does AI MVP development cost and how long does it take?
faqs.answer: The main factors are the number of workflows, data preparation, integrations, access controls and evaluation requirements. A focused pilot with available data differs substantially from a multi-role product connected to several enterprise systems. After discovery, we provide a scope, estimate, milestones and the assumptions that could affect delivery. We also discuss expected ongoing cloud and model costs.

faqs.question: Who owns the product and the accounts?
faqs.answer: Ownership, account access and third-party dependencies are set out in the agreement. The handover should identify the source code, deployment configuration, documentation and evaluation materials you receive. Model services, licensed components and cloud accounts have their own terms, so we make those dependencies visible before they become part of the product.

faqs.question: Can the MVP become a full product after launch?
faqs.answer: Yes, where the pilot evidence supports further investment. The next phase may add capacity, more workflows, stronger operational controls or deeper integrations. Some early components may need revision once actual usage is understood. We provide a roadmap based on those findings rather than promising that every first-release decision will remain suitable at every scale.

faqs.question: Can you improve an existing cloud environment?
faqs.answer: Yes. A project can start with an environment review rather than a migration. We examine the issues you are seeing, such as difficult releases, unclear costs or unreliable integrations, then propose a focused scope. Access and changes follow the approval process agreed with your team.

faqs.question: How do you choose the cloud platform?
faqs.answer: We consider application requirements, existing contracts, team experience, integrations, data location and operating cost. Discovery can assess your existing choice or compare options. We also examine whether part of the system should remain on premises or connect to another cloud. The recommendation explains the workload-specific tradeoffs and what your team must operate.

faqs.question: Will migration interrupt our service?
faqs.answer: Some migrations require a planned interruption; others allow a staged transition. The answer depends on the application's architecture, data synchronization and connected systems. We identify the likely impact during planning, rehearse the sequence where feasible and agree the cutover and rollback decisions before production changes.

faqs.question: What affects implementation cost and timing?
faqs.answer: The main factors are workload count, architecture complexity, data volume, required application changes, security reviews and the available change windows. Cloud usage and third-party licenses are separate from implementation effort. We clarify these costs and assumptions in the proposal after understanding the environment.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee savings or compliance?
faqs.answer: We agree measurable objectives and review the evidence, but savings depend on usage, architecture and service choices. Compliance requirements also extend beyond a cloud configuration. We work with your security or compliance owners to implement the agreed controls and document their responsibilities and acceptance checks.

faqs.question: What should we share to get started?
faqs.answer: Send a brief description of the applications, your current hosting arrangement, the problem you want to solve and any target date. Architecture diagrams, a recent cost summary and known integration dependencies are helpful. Do not send passwords; we agree an appropriate access process when the project is scoped.

faqs.question: Do customers need a script or experience on camera?
faqs.answer: No. We provide topics and open questions so they know what the conversation will cover. The customer describes their own experience, with time to pause or explain something again. We can help structure an answer clearly without supplying a claim or opinion for them to pretend is their own.

faqs.question: Can you film customers in different locations?
faqs.answer: Share the customer locations and availability when you request a proposal. We will confirm workable recording arrangements and any travel or local production requirements before committing to a schedule. Remote recording and customer-supplied footage may be suitable for some stories; the choice depends on the desired quality, setting and available equipment.

faqs.question: How much does testimonial video production cost?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on the number of interviews and locations, recording arrangements, supporting footage, editing complexity and delivery versions. Captions, graphics, translations and review requirements also affect the scope. We quote against an agreed production plan so you can see what is included and what would change the price.

faqs.question: How long should the video be, and how does review work?
faqs.answer: Length follows the story and placement. A short social extract can focus on one useful answer; a website or sales version may need more context. We agree the version list and review milestones before production. Your team names a primary approval contact, and the customer’s review role is confirmed so consolidated feedback can guide revisions.

faqs.question: Can we use the video in ads and create shorter versions?
faqs.answer: Yes, where those uses are covered by the customer permissions and asset licenses. We agree advertising use, channels and cutdowns in advance, then produce versions that retain the meaning and necessary context of the original interview. Any relevant disclosures need to remain clear in the shorter format as well.

faqs.question: Can you edit interviews or customer footage we already have?
faqs.answer: Yes. We first review the recordings, audio, available supporting material and permission to use them. We can then recommend a realistic edit and version plan. If an essential answer or usable recording is missing, we will identify the gap and discuss whether a short additional interview would improve the story.

faqs.question: When should we start pre-launch marketing?
faqs.answer: Start while there is still time to change the message, build the signup journey and learn from the response. The schedule depends on your product readiness, asset needs and approval process. Share the intended release date and current materials with us; we will identify the essential work and whether testing fits the available window.

faqs.question: Can you help if the product is still being built?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can work on audience research, positioning and an early-interest page while development continues. The public message must accurately describe availability and what people are signing up for. Product functionality and release promises stay aligned with your team’s confirmed plans.

faqs.question: What affects the cost of a pre-launch campaign?

faqs.question: How do you measure whether a waitlist is useful?
faqs.answer: We assess whether subscribers match the audience, understand the offer and respond to the next invitation. That may mean confirming interest, joining a beta, booking a demo or buying after release. Source-level conversion and follow-up behavior help explain list quality; signups are an early signal rather than a sales forecast.

faqs.question: Can you work with our existing website and marketing team?

We agree who owns each channel and approval, then use the existing systems where they support the project. Any additional build or integration work is identified before it starts.

faqs.question: What should we share when requesting a proposal?

Include the available budget range and any fixed commitments. We use those details to recommend priorities and explain the tradeoffs within your launch window.

faqs.question: Can you create photography and video in the same project?

faqs.question: Can you work with a brand in the United States or another market?

faqs.question: Can you edit footage we already have?

faqs.question: What do you need from us before production?

faqs.question: How much does B2B video production cost?
